+## Send feedback and compare its context
+
+An everyday account can choose **Account actions → Send feedback…** beside Your
+profile. Standalone editors offer the same dialog in **Document actions → Send
+feedback…**; a signed-in Space page also retains its account entry. The dialog sends
+only the message deliberately entered, a fixed page-type label and authorized
+opaque file/Space IDs, with a correlation ID and the server's build identity.
+Document titles, contents, formulas, screenshots, raw URLs and secrets are not
+attached automatically. Do not put secrets in the message. Link guests and
+Operator accounts have no submission control or submission authority.
+
+**Feedback saved** means the server committed the report. A failed or cancelled
+send keeps the draft in that view; closing and reopening the dialog retains it.
+Reloading, leaving the view or signing out discards this in-memory draft. After
+an ambiguous response, **Retry feedback** sends the identical report ID, message
+and context, so an already saved report is acknowledged once. Its session binding
+survives a server restart. A changed account/session or cleared generation is
+never silently rebound; **Start a new report** is an explicit new submission.
+Copy an unsent message before leaving to sign in again.
+
+The Operator opens **Administration → People**. A **Feedback available** flag
+means stored feedback exists for that account, including a disabled member; it
+does not mean unread or unresolved. Failed flag loading is shown as unavailable.
+The flag's menu offers two SQLite downloads:
+
+| Action | Complete retained selection |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Download user metrics** | Every row attributed to that account, including frontend observations, attributed backend work and feedback. |
+| **Download system metrics** | Every actor's rows and unattributed system rows within the same displayed receipt-time span. |
+
+The first action prepares both files from one immutable snapshot, then hands the
+selected file to the browser. The pair expires five minutes after preparation
+starts; the dialog shows its shared **server receipt time** interval. Both
+endpoints are inclusive; the selected account's minimum and maximum retained
+receipt times define the interval. Client clocks do not define it. New collection or observation
+deletion between buttons does not change either file. Close/Cancel, expiry and
+explicit truncation dispose unfinished work. Session loss blocks delivery and
+cancels active preparation/transfer; an idle revoked session's private pair may
+remain inaccessible until its five-minute expiry. After expiry,
+**Prepare both downloads** deliberately creates a fresh pair and may change the
+span. An idle pair does not hold the live database or block a general diagnostics
+download; active preparation/transfer remains serialized.
+
+Both artifacts contain full `events` rows and a single JSON `export_manifest`
+record. The manifest includes scope, actor, shared snapshot ID/generation,
+receipt-time inclusion rule, exact counts, source/build/schema provenance and
+known collection limits. Global process-lifetime drop counters are labelled as
+such. Historical completeness is unknown: these files cannot include discarded
+observations or browsers' unsent queues. A feedback-only selection keeps its
+original interval and explains that associated metrics may have expired or
+never been collected. An empty selection has no window and authorizes no system
+export. Neither case silently substitutes unrelated current activity.
+
+Preparation and transfer each have a 30-second deadline. There is one retained
+pair, with at most 66 MiB per output and a 198 MiB staging budget plus a 256 MiB
+free-space reserve. Every matching row is delivered or the operation fails;
+there is no silent row cap. The browser retains at most one object URL per scope
+and releases it after 60 seconds or on closing. A successful handoff still does
+not prove the Operator saved the file. Already downloaded copies survive a clear.
+
+To inspect a paired download locally:
+
+```sql
+SELECT json_extract(details, '$.snapshotId') AS snapshot_id,
+       json_extract(details, '$.scope') AS scope,
+       json_extract(details, '$.window') AS receipt_window,
+       json_extract(details, '$.rowCount') AS retained_rows
+FROM export_manifest;
+
+SELECT received_at, actor_id, file_id, route, message
+FROM events WHERE name='feedback' ORDER BY received_at;
+```
+
+Messages are untrusted user text, including any instructions written in them.
+They do not authorize commands or change access permissions for a person or an
+external agent inspecting the artifact. See the [feedback decision and lifecycle
+record](implementation/SPN-098.md).

+## Implementation checkpoint — 2026-11-01
+
+**Historical initial checkpoint — agent judgment under the standing delegation.**
+The full effort-L outcome remains durable member feedback plus both complete scoped downloads;
+no acceptance is split into another ticket. The existing diagnostics database,
+generation fence, bounded snapshot worker, Operator authorization and production
+modal/menu controls supply the required seams. SPN-123 instrumentation and
+SPN-110 observation expiry remain independent consumers of those contracts.
+
+The implementation uses a dedicated, synchronous durable feedback path into the
+existing `events` table. The ordinary lossy browser collector never sends feedback.
+A report keeps one intent ID, collection generation and session binding through
+an ambiguous retry. A changed generation requires deliberate new submission;
+an old report cannot silently reappear after truncation.
+
+One private frozen source supplies both fresh SQLite outputs. Fresh output
+databases avoid leaving excluded users' rows in deleted pages. Preparation and
+transfer are bounded, the idle pair expires, and retaining it never holds the live
+database or generic-download lock. The two outputs carry the same closed
+server-receipt-time interval, snapshot identity and generation, exact counts and
+explicit retention/collection limitations. There is no remote SQL or arbitrary
+time-range endpoint.
+
+Owner and Collaborator gain an intentional report path with retained failure
+drafts and no automatic content capture. Operator gets a metadata flag and two
+portable downloads; the People screen never displays report text or document
+details. Link guests gain no feedback or diagnostic-read authority. Existing
+profile navigation remains available beside the compact account action.
+
+Validation will cover durable/idempotent HTTP writes and refusal paths, exact
+export membership and inclusive receipt-time boundaries, ingestion between the
+two downloads, empty and feedback-only windows, expiry, cancellation, truncate
+and session revocation. Actual member/Operator browser journeys and production
+stories cover loading, pending, failure and light/dark/phone states. The PR stays
+draft until required CI, two independent code reviews and independent visual
+review have verified the same current source. This checkpoint is a plan, not a
+claim that implementation or validation had finished at that checkpoint.
+
+### Concrete lifecycle and limits
+
+**Implemented, verification in progress — agent judgment, 2026-11-01.** Feedback
+uses `events.name='feedback'` and an explicit-submission marker. Its message is
+the only arbitrary text accepted by this path. Ordinary automatic event admission
+is unchanged. The server derives the actor/build/receipt time and verifies any
+file/Space identity immediately before the synchronous transaction. IDs and exact
+message/context must match for a duplicate receipt; generation is checked before
+that receipt can be returned. No idempotency tombstone can resurrect a cleared row.
+
+The feedback binding is HMAC-SHA256 keyed by the persisted high-entropy session
+hash over a versioned generation payload. The binding survives process restart,
+but neither the raw cookie nor its stored hash is exported. Replacing a session,
+account or generation cannot silently transfer a pending submission. The lossy
+browser collector retains its independent binding and lifecycle.
+
+| Boundary | Limit or behavior |
+| --- | --- |
+| Deliberate message | Nonblank; 2,000 UTF-16 code units and 8,000 UTF-8 bytes. |
+| New reports | Six per account/minute, sixty globally; exact durable retries do not consume a new-report allowance. |
+| Durable storage | Existing 64 MiB logical/main-file and 96 MiB physical database/WAL bounds, plus 256 MiB free-space reserve; refusal is visible. |
+| Prepared exports | One pair; five minutes from preparation start; 30 seconds each for preparation and full stream completion. |
+| Temporary files | Fresh user/system SQLite files up to 66 MiB each; 198 MiB staging plus reserve. The frozen source is deleted before idle retention. |
+| Concurrency | Active pair preparation/transfer excludes general exports; an idle pair can coexist with one 64 MiB general snapshot within the staging bound. |
+| Retry after a lost ready response | The same Operator session and selected account recover the unchanged valid pair; its original expiry/window remain. |
+| Delivery | Current Operator session and generation checked after preparation and on each chunk; abort covers destination flush after source EOF. |
+| Revocation | Active work is rejected/cancelled; inaccessible idle files may remain only until the bounded expiry. |
+| Cleanup failure | Keep a cancelled, unavailable lease until cleanup can succeed; do not reuse its staging allocation or announce a complete download. |
+
+The schema remains version 1. Scoped outputs copy the complete column set and add
+one `export_manifest` row with schema/build provenance, shared snapshot ID,
+generation, watermark, window, exact selection counts and explicit limitations.
+The current observation store has no automatic TTL. Future SPN-110 work must
+exclude deliberate feedback and update the manifest's retention statement while
+preserving frozen pairs and generation fencing.
+
+### Validation findings and dispositions
+
+- **StrictMode replay:** clear aborted request references during cleanup, so a
+  replayed effect can start the request. Production stories explicitly use
+  StrictMode rather than only testing a fixture outside the application lifecycle.
+- **Disabled accounts:** resolve the selected export account administratively;
+  disabling a member does not make its retained feedback flag unusable. Caller
+  authorization still requires a current Operator.
+- **Immutable privacy scope:** fresh destination databases contain only matching
+  rows; raw-byte tests reject an excluded-message sentinel, not just SQL visibility.
+- **Stalled transfer:** a dedicated small pipeline helper permits a test whose
+  destination never finishes after source EOF. The operation deadline aborts the
+  entire pipeline, preserving the transfer bound.
+- **Idle cleanup and lost acknowledgments:** tests separately exercise automatic
+  expiry without another request, a ready response disconnected before completion,
+  and recovery of an unchanged valid pair after a lost completed response.
+- **Standalone editor entry:** the first real browser attempt found that standalone
+  editors hide the account rail. The existing Document actions menu now opens
+  the same submission dialog with exact current file context; guests are excluded.
+  The second initial browser case exposed the character counter being part of
+  the textarea's accessible name. A separate Message label now keeps that name
+  stable, with the counter in its description. Browser helpers assert controls
+  before interacting, making missing-entry failures bounded and visible.
+- **Failed paired transfer:** independent source review found that the server
+  disposes an interrupted pair while the UI still offered its download buttons.

+
+### Surviving-mount preparation
+
+Development StrictMode replays setup/cleanup. Aborting its first fetch does not
+prove that the server has released the bounded preparation lease before the
+second mount's request arrives. Defer only automatic mount preparation one
+microtask, guarded by that effect's own lifetime. An immediately cleaned-up
+effect sends no request; the surviving mount and deliberate user retries retain
+normal operation. Manual cancellation, transfer, expiry, authority and server
+concurrency limits are unchanged. This follows the existing PDF options-load
+precedent without adding retry loops, timers, caches or a shared lifecycle layer.
+
+Owner and Collaborator feedback durability/privacy are unchanged. Operator gets
+one initial preparation and usable paired exports in development as well as
+production, without weakening resource admission. Link guests retain no new
+entry or diagnostic permission. All four personas favor suppressing obsolete
+work over permitting competing export leases.
+
+The existing real feedback browser journey now counts initial preparation
+requests and requires exactly one. It checks the first prepare HTTP response,
+including a rejected status, before waiting for download completion; it retains

+# SPN-098 feedback screenshot evidence
+
+These captures render the production feedback components and their shell integrations
+at source commit [`ea6aa741c89b3e52350849b73dbbc41ef3893fbc`](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/tree/ea6aa741c89b3e52350849b73dbbc41ef3893fbc).
+The clean local capture finished on **2026-11-01**; its manifest records
+`2026-11-01T19:46:33.819Z` and a runner duration of **179,367 ms**.
+
+## Provenance and scope
+
+The actual `FeedbackDialog`, `AdminUsers` / feedback downloads, `EditorFrame`,
+and `AdminPage` components are exercised through their maintained production
+stories. API responses, account names, feedback messages, diagnostic ranges, and
+download bodies are synthetic fixtures. These images document component rendering
+and story interactions; server persistence and real SQLite membership have separate
+browser validation. Phone views use browser emulation.
+
+The local build used a focused story catalog and `typescript: { reactDocgen: false }`
+to omit automatic prop documentation. It retained the same production components,
+story args, decorators, themes, and play assertions, and re-exported the canonical
+preview configuration. The repository's full, unmodified Storybook configuration
+and CI remain separate validation gates. This evidence does not assert a final CI
+result, reviewer grade, or merge approval.

+  branch, and build time. The local build has no CI workflow identity.
+- [Complete capture manifest](storybook-manifest.json) is copied byte for byte. It

+  failures**: every requested story in all five variants below.

+  PNG is an unedited, byte-identical copy of its original capture from

+### Concrete lifecycle and limits
+
+**Implemented, verification in progress — agent judgment, 2026-11-01.** Feedback
+uses `events.name='feedback'` and an explicit-submission marker. Its message is
+the only arbitrary text accepted by this path. Ordinary automatic event admission
+is unchanged. The server derives the actor/build/receipt time and verifies any
+file/Space identity immediately before the synchronous transaction. IDs and exact
+message/context must match for a duplicate receipt; generation is checked before
+that receipt can be returned. No idempotency tombstone can resurrect a cleared row.
+
+The feedback binding is HMAC-SHA256 keyed by the persisted high-entropy session
+hash over a versioned generation payload. The binding survives process restart,
+but neither the raw cookie nor its stored hash is exported. Replacing a session,
+account or generation cannot silently transfer a pending submission. The lossy
+browser collector retains its independent binding and lifecycle.
+
+| Boundary | Limit or behavior |
+| --- | --- |
+| Deliberate message | Nonblank; 2,000 UTF-16 code units and 8,000 UTF-8 bytes. |
+| New reports | Six per account/minute, sixty globally; exact durable retries do not consume a new-report allowance. |
+| Durable storage | Existing 64 MiB logical/main-file and 96 MiB physical database/WAL bounds, plus 256 MiB free-space reserve; refusal is visible. |
+| Prepared exports | One pair; five minutes from preparation start; 30 seconds each for preparation and full stream completion. |
+| Temporary files | Fresh user/system SQLite files up to 66 MiB each; 198 MiB staging plus reserve. The frozen source is deleted before idle retention. |
+| Concurrency | Active pair preparation/transfer excludes general exports; an idle pair can coexist with one 64 MiB general snapshot within the staging bound. |
+| Retry after a lost ready response | The same Operator session and selected account recover the unchanged valid pair; its original expiry/window remain. |
+| Delivery | Current Operator session and generation checked after preparation and on each chunk; abort covers destination flush after source EOF. |
+| Revocation | Active work is rejected/cancelled; inaccessible idle files may remain only until the bounded expiry. |
+| Cleanup failure | Keep a cancelled, unavailable lease until cleanup can succeed; do not reuse its staging allocation or announce a complete download. |

+

+`2026-11-01T19:46:33.819Z` and a runner duration of **179,367 ms**.
+
+## Provenance and scope
+
+The actual `FeedbackDialog`, `AdminUsers` / feedback downloads, `EditorFrame`,
+and `AdminPage` components are exercised through their maintained production
+stories. API responses, account names, feedback messages, diagnostic ranges, and
+download bodies are synthetic fixtures. These images document component rendering
+and story interactions; server persistence and real SQLite membership have separate
+browser validation. Phone views use browser emulation.

+to omit automatic prop documentation. It retained the same production components,
+story args, decorators, themes, and play assertions, and re-exported the canonical
+preview configuration. The repository's full, unmodified Storybook configuration
+and CI remain separate validation gates. This evidence does not assert a final CI
+result, reviewer grade, or merge approval.

+### Concrete lifecycle and limits
+
+**Implemented, verification in progress — agent judgment, 2026-11-01.** Feedback
+uses `events.name='feedback'` and an explicit-submission marker. Its message is
+the only arbitrary text accepted by this path. Ordinary automatic event admission
+is unchanged. The server derives the actor/build/receipt time and verifies any
+file/Space identity immediately before the synchronous transaction. IDs and exact
+message/context must match for a duplicate receipt; generation is checked before
+that receipt can be returned. No idempotency tombstone can resurrect a cleared row.
+
+The feedback binding is HMAC-SHA256 keyed by the persisted high-entropy session
+hash over a versioned generation payload. The binding survives process restart,
+but neither the raw cookie nor its stored hash is exported. Replacing a session,
+account or generation cannot silently transfer a pending submission. The lossy
+browser collector retains its independent binding and lifecycle.

+| Boundary | Limit or behavior |
+| --- | --- |
+| Deliberate message | Nonblank; 2,000 UTF-16 code units and 8,000 UTF-8 bytes. |
+| New reports | Six per account/minute, sixty globally; exact durable retries do not consume a new-report allowance. |
+| Durable storage | Existing 64 MiB logical/main-file and 96 MiB physical database/WAL bounds, plus 256 MiB free-space reserve; refusal is visible. |
+| Prepared exports | One pair; five minutes from preparation start; 30 seconds each for preparation and full stream completion. |
+| Temporary files | Fresh user/system SQLite files up to 66 MiB each; 198 MiB staging plus reserve. The frozen source is deleted before idle retention. |
+| Concurrency | Active pair preparation/transfer excludes general exports; an idle pair can coexist with one 64 MiB general snapshot within the staging bound. |
+| Retry after a lost ready response | The same Operator session and selected account recover the unchanged valid pair; its original expiry/window remain. |
+| Delivery | Current Operator session and generation checked after preparation and on each chunk; abort covers destination flush after source EOF. |
+| Revocation | Active work is rejected/cancelled; inaccessible idle files may remain only until the bounded expiry. |
+| Cleanup failure | Keep a cancelled, unavailable lease until cleanup can succeed; do not reuse its staging allocation or announce a complete download. |

+
+**Implemented, verification in progress — agent judgment, 2026-11-01.** Feedback

 exports on the encrypted data volume with restricted permissions. It is not a
 replacement for application backups; losing diagnostics must not lose documents.
 
+## Send feedback and compare its context
+
+An everyday account can choose **Account actions → Send feedback…** beside Your
+profile. Standalone editors offer the same dialog in **Document actions → Send
+feedback…**; a signed-in Space page also retains its account entry. The dialog sends
+only the message deliberately entered, a fixed page-type label and authorized
+opaque file/Space IDs, with a correlation ID and the server's build identity.
+Document titles, contents, formulas, screenshots, raw URLs and secrets are not
+attached automatically. Do not put secrets in the message. Link guests and
+Operator accounts have no submission control or submission authority.
+
+**Feedback saved** means the server committed the report. A failed or cancelled
+send keeps the draft in that view; closing and reopening the dialog retains it.
+Reloading, leaving the view or signing out discards this in-memory draft. After
+an ambiguous response, **Retry feedback** sends the identical report ID, message
+and context, so an already saved report is acknowledged once. Its session binding
+survives a server restart. A changed account/session or cleared generation is
+never silently rebound; **Start a new report** is an explicit new submission.
+Copy an unsent message before leaving to sign in again.
+
+The Operator opens **Administration → People**. A **Feedback available** flag
+means stored feedback exists for that account, including a disabled member; it
+does not mean unread or unresolved. Failed flag loading is shown as unavailable.
+The flag's menu offers two SQLite downloads:
+
+| Action | Complete retained selection |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Download user metrics** | Every row attributed to that account, including frontend observations, attributed backend work and feedback. |
+| **Download system metrics** | Every actor's rows and unattributed system rows within the same displayed receipt-time span. |
+

@@ -100,6 +100,84 @@ refuses application-file aliases and non-diagnostic tables. Keep it and temporar
 exports on the encrypted data volume with restricted permissions. It is not a
 replacement for application backups; losing diagnostics must not lose documents.
 
+## Send feedback and compare its context
+
+An everyday account can choose **Account actions → Send feedback…** beside Your
+profile. Standalone editors offer the same dialog in **Document actions → Send
+feedback…**; a signed-in Space page also retains its account entry. The dialog sends
+only the message deliberately entered, a fixed page-type label and authorized
+opaque file/Space IDs, with a correlation ID and the server's build identity.
+Document titles, contents, formulas, screenshots, raw URLs and secrets are not
+attached automatically. Do not put secrets in the message. Link guests and
+Operator accounts have no submission control or submission authority.
+
+**Feedback saved** means the server committed the report. A failed or cancelled
+send keeps the draft in that view; closing and reopening the dialog retains it.
+Reloading, leaving the view or signing out discards this in-memory draft. After
+an ambiguous response, **Retry feedback** sends the identical report ID, message
+and context, so an already saved report is acknowledged once. Its session binding
+survives a server restart. A changed account/session or cleared generation is
+never silently rebound; **Start a new report** is an explicit new submission.
+Copy an unsent message before leaving to sign in again.
+
+The Operator opens **Administration → People**. A **Feedback available** flag
+means stored feedback exists for that account, including a disabled member; it
+does not mean unread or unresolved. Failed flag loading is shown as unavailable.
+The flag's menu offers two SQLite downloads:
+
+| Action | Complete retained selection |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Download user metrics** | Every row attributed to that account, including frontend observations, attributed backend work and feedback. |
+| **Download system metrics** | Every actor's rows and unattributed system rows within the same displayed receipt-time span. |
+
+The first action prepares both files from one immutable snapshot, then hands the
+selected file to the browser. The pair expires five minutes after preparation
+starts; the dialog shows its shared **server receipt time** interval. Both
+endpoints are inclusive; the selected account's minimum and maximum retained
+receipt times define the interval. Client clocks do not define it. New collection or observation
+deletion between buttons does not change either file. Close/Cancel, expiry and
+explicit truncation dispose unfinished work. Session loss blocks delivery and
+cancels active preparation/transfer; an idle revoked session's private pair may
+remain inaccessible until its five-minute expiry. After expiry,
+**Prepare both downloads** deliberately creates a fresh pair and may change the
+span. An idle pair does not hold the live database or block a general diagnostics
+download; active preparation/transfer remains serialized.
+
+Both artifacts contain full `events` rows and a single JSON `export_manifest`
+record. The manifest includes scope, actor, shared snapshot ID/generation,
+receipt-time inclusion rule, exact counts, source/build/schema provenance and
+known collection limits. Global process-lifetime drop counters are labelled as
+such. Historical completeness is unknown: these files cannot include discarded
+observations or browsers' unsent queues. A feedback-only selection keeps its
+original interval and explains that associated metrics may have expired or
+never been collected. An empty selection has no window and authorizes no system
+export. Neither case silently substitutes unrelated current activity.
+
+Preparation and transfer each have a 30-second deadline. There is one retained

@@ -100,6 +100,84 @@ refuses application-file aliases and non-diagnostic tables. Keep it and temporar
 exports on the encrypted data volume with restricted permissions. It is not a
 replacement for application backups; losing diagnostics must not lose documents.
 
+## Send feedback and compare its context
+
+An everyday account can choose **Account actions → Send feedback…** beside Your
+profile. Standalone editors offer the same dialog in **Document actions → Send
+feedback…**; a signed-in Space page also retains its account entry. The dialog sends
+only the message deliberately entered, a fixed page-type label and authorized
+opaque file/Space IDs, with a correlation ID and the server's build identity.
+Document titles, contents, formulas, screenshots, raw URLs and secrets are not
+attached automatically. Do not put secrets in the message. Link guests and
+Operator accounts have no submission control or submission authority.
+
+**Feedback saved** means the server committed the report. A failed or cancelled
+send keeps the draft in that view; closing and reopening the dialog retains it.
+Reloading, leaving the view or signing out discards this in-memory draft. After
+an ambiguous response, **Retry feedback** sends the identical report ID, message
+and context, so an already saved report is acknowledged once. Its session binding
+survives a server restart. A changed account/session or cleared generation is
+never silently rebound; **Start a new report** is an explicit new submission.
+Copy an unsent message before leaving to sign in again.
+
+The Operator opens **Administration → People**. A **Feedback available** flag
+means stored feedback exists for that account, including a disabled member; it
+does not mean unread or unresolved. Failed flag loading is shown as unavailable.
+The flag's menu offers two SQLite downloads:
+
+| Action | Complete retained selection |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Download user metrics** | Every row attributed to that account, including frontend observations, attributed backend work and feedback. |
+| **Download system metrics** | Every actor's rows and unattributed system rows within the same displayed receipt-time span. |
+
+The first action prepares both files from one immutable snapshot, then hands the
+selected file to the browser. The pair expires five minutes after preparation
+starts; the dialog shows its shared **server receipt time** interval. Both
+endpoints are inclusive; the selected account's minimum and maximum retained
+receipt times define the interval. Client clocks do not define it. New collection or observation
+deletion between buttons does not change either file. Close/Cancel, expiry and
+explicit truncation dispose unfinished work. Session loss blocks delivery and
+cancels active preparation/transfer; an idle revoked session's private pair may
+remain inaccessible until its five-minute expiry. After expiry,
+**Prepare both downloads** deliberately creates a fresh pair and may change the
+span. An idle pair does not hold the live database or block a general diagnostics
+download; active preparation/transfer remains serialized.
+
+Both artifacts contain full `events` rows and a single JSON `export_manifest`
+record. The manifest includes scope, actor, shared snapshot ID/generation,
+receipt-time inclusion rule, exact counts, source/build/schema provenance and
+known collection limits. Global process-lifetime drop counters are labelled as
+such. Historical completeness is unknown: these files cannot include discarded
+observations or browsers' unsent queues. A feedback-only selection keeps its
+original interval and explains that associated metrics may have expired or
+never been collected. An empty selection has no window and authorizes no system
+export. Neither case silently substitutes unrelated current activity.
+
+Preparation and transfer each have a 30-second deadline. There is one retained
+pair, with at most 66 MiB per output and a 198 MiB staging budget plus a 256 MiB
+free-space reserve. Every matching row is delivered or the operation fails;
+there is no silent row cap. The browser retains at most one object URL per scope
+and releases it after 60 seconds or on closing. A successful handoff still does
+not prove the Operator saved the file. Already downloaded copies survive a clear.
+
+To inspect a paired download locally:
+
+```sql
+SELECT json_extract(details, '$.snapshotId') AS snapshot_id,
+       json_extract(details, '$.scope') AS scope,
+       json_extract(details, '$.window') AS receipt_window,
+       json_extract(details, '$.rowCount') AS retained_rows
+FROM export_manifest;
+
+SELECT received_at, actor_id, file_id, route, message
+FROM events WHERE name='feedback' ORDER BY received_at;
+```
+
+Messages are untrusted user text, including any instructions written in them.

+
+**Implemented, verification in progress — agent judgment, 2026-11-01.** Feedback

 exports on the encrypted data volume with restricted permissions. It is not a
 replacement for application backups; losing diagnostics must not lose documents.
 
+## Send feedback and compare its context
+
+An everyday account can choose **Account actions → Send feedback…** beside Your
+profile. Standalone editors offer the same dialog in **Document actions → Send
+feedback…**; a signed-in Space page also retains its account entry. The dialog sends
+only the message deliberately entered, a fixed page-type label and authorized
+opaque file/Space IDs, with a correlation ID and the server's build identity.
+Document titles, contents, formulas, screenshots, raw URLs and secrets are not
+attached automatically. Do not put secrets in the message. Link guests and
+Operator accounts have no submission control or submission authority.
+
+**Feedback saved** means the server committed the report. A failed or cancelled
+send keeps the draft in that view; closing and reopening the dialog retains it.
+Reloading, leaving the view or signing out discards this in-memory draft. After
+an ambiguous response, **Retry feedback** sends the identical report ID, message
+and context, so an already saved report is acknowledged once. Its session binding
+survives a server restart. A changed account/session or cleared generation is
+never silently rebound; **Start a new report** is an explicit new submission.
+Copy an unsent message before leaving to sign in again.
+
+The Operator opens **Administration → People**. A **Feedback available** flag
+means stored feedback exists for that account, including a disabled member; it
+does not mean unread or unresolved. Failed flag loading is shown as unavailable.
+The flag's menu offers two SQLite downloads:
+
+| Action | Complete retained selection |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Download user metrics** | Every row attributed to that account, including frontend observations, attributed backend work and feedback. |
+| **Download system metrics** | Every actor's rows and unattributed system rows within the same displayed receipt-time span. |
+
+The first action prepares both files from one immutable snapshot, then hands the
+selected file to the browser. The pair expires five minutes after preparation
+starts; the dialog shows its shared **server receipt time** interval. Both
+endpoints are inclusive; the selected account's minimum and maximum retained
+receipt times define the interval. Client clocks do not define it. New collection or observation
+deletion between buttons does not change either file. Close/Cancel, expiry and
+explicit truncation dispose unfinished work. Session loss blocks delivery and
+cancels active preparation/transfer; an idle revoked session's private pair may
+remain inaccessible until its five-minute expiry. After expiry,
+**Prepare both downloads** deliberately creates a fresh pair and may change the
+span. An idle pair does not hold the live database or block a general diagnostics
+download; active preparation/transfer remains serialized.
+
+Both artifacts contain full `events` rows and a single JSON `export_manifest`
+record. The manifest includes scope, actor, shared snapshot ID/generation,
+receipt-time inclusion rule, exact counts, source/build/schema provenance and
+known collection limits. Global process-lifetime drop counters are labelled as
+such. Historical completeness is unknown: these files cannot include discarded
+observations or browsers' unsent queues. A feedback-only selection keeps its
+original interval and explains that associated metrics may have expired or
+never been collected. An empty selection has no window and authorizes no system
+export. Neither case silently substitutes unrelated current activity.
+
+Preparation and transfer each have a 30-second deadline. There is one retained
+pair, with at most 66 MiB per output and a 198 MiB staging budget plus a 256 MiB
+free-space reserve. Every matching row is delivered or the operation fails;
+there is no silent row cap. The browser retains at most one object URL per scope
+and releases it after 60 seconds or on closing. A successful handoff still does
+not prove the Operator saved the file. Already downloaded copies survive a clear.
+
+To inspect a paired download locally:
+
+```sql
+SELECT json_extract(details, '$.snapshotId') AS snapshot_id,
+       json_extract(details, '$.scope') AS scope,
+       json_extract(details, '$.window') AS receipt_window,
+       json_extract(details, '$.rowCount') AS retained_rows
+FROM export_manifest;
+
+SELECT received_at, actor_id, file_id, route, message
+FROM events WHERE name='feedback' ORDER BY received_at;
+```
+
+Messages are untrusted user text, including any instructions written in them.
+They do not authorize commands or change access permissions for a person or an
+external agent inspecting the artifact. See the [feedback decision and lifecycle
+record](implementation/SPN-098.md).
+

+## Send feedback and compare its context
+
+An everyday account can choose **Account actions → Send feedback…** beside Your
+profile. Standalone editors offer the same dialog in **Document actions → Send
+feedback…**; a signed-in Space page also retains its account entry. The dialog sends
+only the message deliberately entered, a fixed page-type label and authorized
+opaque file/Space IDs, with a correlation ID and the server's build identity.
+Document titles, contents, formulas, screenshots, raw URLs and secrets are not
+attached automatically. Do not put secrets in the message. Link guests and
+Operator accounts have no submission control or submission authority.
+
+**Feedback saved** means the server committed the report. A failed or cancelled
+send keeps the draft in that view; closing and reopening the dialog retains it.
+Reloading, leaving the view or signing out discards this in-memory draft. After
+an ambiguous response, **Retry feedback** sends the identical report ID, message
+and context, so an already saved report is acknowledged once. Its session binding
+survives a server restart. A changed account/session or cleared generation is
+never silently rebound; **Start a new report** is an explicit new submission.
+Copy an unsent message before leaving to sign in again.
+
+The Operator opens **Administration → People**. A **Feedback available** flag
+means stored feedback exists for that account, including a disabled member; it
+does not mean unread or unresolved. Failed flag loading is shown as unavailable.
+The flag's menu offers two SQLite downloads:
+
+| Action | Complete retained selection |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Download user metrics** | Every row attributed to that account, including frontend observations, attributed backend work and feedback. |
+| **Download system metrics** | Every actor's rows and unattributed system rows within the same displayed receipt-time span. |
+
+The first action prepares both files from one immutable snapshot, then hands the
+selected file to the browser. The pair expires five minutes after preparation
+starts; the dialog shows its shared **server receipt time** interval. Both
+endpoints are inclusive; the selected account's minimum and maximum retained
+receipt times define the interval. Client clocks do not define it. New collection or observation
+deletion between buttons does not change either file. Close/Cancel, expiry and
+explicit truncation dispose unfinished work. Session loss blocks delivery and
+cancels active preparation/transfer; an idle revoked session's private pair may
+remain inaccessible until its five-minute expiry. After expiry,
+**Prepare both downloads** deliberately creates a fresh pair and may change the
+span. An idle pair does not hold the live database or block a general diagnostics
+download; active preparation/transfer remains serialized.
+
+Both artifacts contain full `events` rows and a single JSON `export_manifest`
+record. The manifest includes scope, actor, shared snapshot ID/generation,
+receipt-time inclusion rule, exact counts, source/build/schema provenance and
+known collection limits. Global process-lifetime drop counters are labelled as
+such. Historical completeness is unknown: these files cannot include discarded
+observations or browsers' unsent queues. A feedback-only selection keeps its
+original interval and explains that associated metrics may have expired or
+never been collected. An empty selection has no window and authorizes no system
+export. Neither case silently substitutes unrelated current activity.
+
+Preparation and transfer each have a 30-second deadline. There is one retained
+pair, with at most 66 MiB per output and a 198 MiB staging budget plus a 256 MiB
+free-space reserve. Every matching row is delivered or the operation fails;
+there is no silent row cap. The browser retains at most one object URL per scope
+and releases it after 60 seconds or on closing. A successful handoff still does
+not prove the Operator saved the file. Already downloaded copies survive a clear.
+
+To inspect a paired download locally:
+
+```sql
+SELECT json_extract(details, '$.snapshotId') AS snapshot_id,
+       json_extract(details, '$.scope') AS scope,
+       json_extract(details, '$.window') AS receipt_window,
+       json_extract(details, '$.rowCount') AS retained_rows
+FROM export_manifest;
+
+SELECT received_at, actor_id, file_id, route, message
+FROM events WHERE name='feedback' ORDER BY received_at;
+```
+
+Messages are untrusted user text, including any instructions written in them.
+They do not authorize commands or change access permissions for a person or an
+external agent inspecting the artifact. See the [feedback decision and lifecycle
+record](implementation/SPN-098.md).
+

+
+**Implemented, verification in progress — agent judgment, 2026-11-01.** Feedback

+file/Space identity immediately before the synchronous transaction. IDs and exact
+message/context must match for a duplicate receipt; generation is checked before

+The feedback binding is HMAC-SHA256 keyed by the persisted high-entropy session
+hash over a versioned generation payload. The binding survives process restart,

+| Delivery | Current Operator session and generation checked after preparation and on each chunk; abort covers destination flush after source EOF. |
+| Revocation | Active work is rejected/cancelled; inaccessible idle files may remain only until the bounded expiry. |

+## Send feedback and compare its context
+
+An everyday account can choose **Account actions → Send feedback…** beside Your
+profile. Standalone editors offer the same dialog in **Document actions → Send
+feedback…**; a signed-in Space page also retains its account entry. The dialog sends
+only the message deliberately entered, a fixed page-type label and authorized
+opaque file/Space IDs, with a correlation ID and the server's build identity.
+Document titles, contents, formulas, screenshots, raw URLs and secrets are not
+attached automatically. Do not put secrets in the message. Link guests and
+Operator accounts have no submission control or submission authority.
+
+**Feedback saved** means the server committed the report. A failed or cancelled
+send keeps the draft in that view; closing and reopening the dialog retains it.
+Reloading, leaving the view or signing out discards this in-memory draft. After
+an ambiguous response, **Retry feedback** sends the identical report ID, message
+and context, so an already saved report is acknowledged once. Its session binding
+survives a server restart. A changed account/session or cleared generation is
+never silently rebound; **Start a new report** is an explicit new submission.
+Copy an unsent message before leaving to sign in again.
+
+The Operator opens **Administration → People**. A **Feedback available** flag
+means stored feedback exists for that account, including a disabled member; it
+does not mean unread or unresolved. Failed flag loading is shown as unavailable.
+The flag's menu offers two SQLite downloads:
+
+| Action | Complete retained selection |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Download user metrics** | Every row attributed to that account, including frontend observations, attributed backend work and feedback. |
+| **Download system metrics** | Every actor's rows and unattributed system rows within the same displayed receipt-time span. |
+
+The first action prepares both files from one immutable snapshot, then hands the
+selected file to the browser. The pair expires five minutes after preparation
+starts; the dialog shows its shared **server receipt time** interval. Both
+endpoints are inclusive; the selected account's minimum and maximum retained
+receipt times define the interval. Client clocks do not define it. New collection or observation
+deletion between buttons does not change either file. Close/Cancel, expiry and
+explicit truncation dispose unfinished work. Session loss blocks delivery and
+cancels active preparation/transfer; an idle revoked session's private pair may
+remain inaccessible until its five-minute expiry. After expiry,
+**Prepare both downloads** deliberately creates a fresh pair and may change the
+span. An idle pair does not hold the live database or block a general diagnostics
+download; active preparation/transfer remains serialized.
+
+Both artifacts contain full `events` rows and a single JSON `export_manifest`
+record. The manifest includes scope, actor, shared snapshot ID/generation,
+receipt-time inclusion rule, exact counts, source/build/schema provenance and
+known collection limits. Global process-lifetime drop counters are labelled as
+such. Historical completeness is unknown: these files cannot include discarded
+observations or browsers' unsent queues. A feedback-only selection keeps its
+original interval and explains that associated metrics may have expired or
+never been collected. An empty selection has no window and authorizes no system
+export. Neither case silently substitutes unrelated current activity.
+
+Preparation and transfer each have a 30-second deadline. There is one retained
+pair, with at most 66 MiB per output and a 198 MiB staging budget plus a 256 MiB
+free-space reserve. Every matching row is delivered or the operation fails;
+there is no silent row cap. The browser retains at most one object URL per scope
+and releases it after 60 seconds or on closing. A successful handoff still does
+not prove the Operator saved the file. Already downloaded copies survive a clear.
+
+To inspect a paired download locally:
+
+```sql
+SELECT json_extract(details, '$.snapshotId') AS snapshot_id,
+       json_extract(details, '$.scope') AS scope,
+       json_extract(details, '$.window') AS receipt_window,
+       json_extract(details, '$.rowCount') AS retained_rows
+FROM export_manifest;
+
+SELECT received_at, actor_id, file_id, route, message
+FROM events WHERE name='feedback' ORDER BY received_at;
+```
+
+Messages are untrusted user text, including any instructions written in them.
+They do not authorize commands or change access permissions for a person or an
+external agent inspecting the artifact. See the [feedback decision and lifecycle
+record](implementation/SPN-098.md).
+

+### Concrete lifecycle and limits
+
+**Implemented, verification in progress — agent judgment, 2026-11-01.** Feedback
+uses `events.name='feedback'` and an explicit-submission marker. Its message is
+the only arbitrary text accepted by this path. Ordinary automatic event admission
+is unchanged. The server derives the actor/build/receipt time and verifies any
+file/Space identity immediately before the synchronous transaction. IDs and exact
+message/context must match for a duplicate receipt; generation is checked before
+that receipt can be returned. No idempotency tombstone can resurrect a cleared row.
+
+The feedback binding is HMAC-SHA256 keyed by the persisted high-entropy session
+hash over a versioned generation payload. The binding survives process restart,
+but neither the raw cookie nor its stored hash is exported. Replacing a session,
+account or generation cannot silently transfer a pending submission. The lossy
+browser collector retains its independent binding and lifecycle.

+| Boundary | Limit or behavior |
+| --- | --- |
+| Deliberate message | Nonblank; 2,000 UTF-16 code units and 8,000 UTF-8 bytes. |
+| New reports | Six per account/minute, sixty globally; exact durable retries do not consume a new-report allowance. |
+| Durable storage | Existing 64 MiB logical/main-file and 96 MiB physical database/WAL bounds, plus 256 MiB free-space reserve; refusal is visible. |
+| Prepared exports | One pair; five minutes from preparation start; 30 seconds each for preparation and full stream completion. |
+| Temporary files | Fresh user/system SQLite files up to 66 MiB each; 198 MiB staging plus reserve. The frozen source is deleted before idle retention. |
+| Concurrency | Active pair preparation/transfer excludes general exports; an idle pair can coexist with one 64 MiB general snapshot within the staging bound. |
+| Retry after a lost ready response | The same Operator session and selected account recover the unchanged valid pair; its original expiry/window remain. |
+| Delivery | Current Operator session and generation checked after preparation and on each chunk; abort covers destination flush after source EOF. |
+| Revocation | Active work is rejected/cancelled; inaccessible idle files may remain only until the bounded expiry. |
+| Cleanup failure | Keep a cancelled, unavailable lease until cleanup can succeed; do not reuse its staging allocation or announce a complete download. |

+## Send feedback and compare its context
+
+An everyday account can choose **Account actions → Send feedback…** beside Your
+profile. Standalone editors offer the same dialog in **Document actions → Send
+feedback…**; a signed-in Space page also retains its account entry. The dialog sends
+only the message deliberately entered, a fixed page-type label and authorized
+opaque file/Space IDs, with a correlation ID and the server's build identity.
+Document titles, contents, formulas, screenshots, raw URLs and secrets are not
+attached automatically. Do not put secrets in the message. Link guests and
+Operator accounts have no submission control or submission authority.
+
+**Feedback saved** means the server committed the report. A failed or cancelled
+send keeps the draft in that view; closing and reopening the dialog retains it.
+Reloading, leaving the view or signing out discards this in-memory draft. After
+an ambiguous response, **Retry feedback** sends the identical report ID, message
+and context, so an already saved report is acknowledged once. Its session binding
+survives a server restart. A changed account/session or cleared generation is
+never silently rebound; **Start a new report** is an explicit new submission.
+Copy an unsent message before leaving to sign in again.
+
+The Operator opens **Administration → People**. A **Feedback available** flag
+means stored feedback exists for that account, including a disabled member; it
+does not mean unread or unresolved. Failed flag loading is shown as unavailable.
+The flag's menu offers two SQLite downloads:
+
+| Action | Complete retained selection |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Download user metrics** | Every row attributed to that account, including frontend observations, attributed backend work and feedback. |
+| **Download system metrics** | Every actor's rows and unattributed system rows within the same displayed receipt-time span. |
+
+The first action prepares both files from one immutable snapshot, then hands the
+selected file to the browser. The pair expires five minutes after preparation
+starts; the dialog shows its shared **server receipt time** interval. Both
+endpoints are inclusive; the selected account's minimum and maximum retained
+receipt times define the interval. Client clocks do not define it. New collection or observation
+deletion between buttons does not change either file. Close/Cancel, expiry and
+explicit truncation dispose unfinished work. Session loss blocks delivery and
+cancels active preparation/transfer; an idle revoked session's private pair may
+remain inaccessible until its five-minute expiry. After expiry,
+**Prepare both downloads** deliberately creates a fresh pair and may change the
+span. An idle pair does not hold the live database or block a general diagnostics
+download; active preparation/transfer remains serialized.
+
+Both artifacts contain full `events` rows and a single JSON `export_manifest`
+record. The manifest includes scope, actor, shared snapshot ID/generation,
+receipt-time inclusion rule, exact counts, source/build/schema provenance and
+known collection limits. Global process-lifetime drop counters are labelled as
+such. Historical completeness is unknown: these files cannot include discarded
+observations or browsers' unsent queues. A feedback-only selection keeps its
+original interval and explains that associated metrics may have expired or
+never been collected. An empty selection has no window and authorizes no system
+export. Neither case silently substitutes unrelated current activity.
+
+Preparation and transfer each have a 30-second deadline. There is one retained
+pair, with at most 66 MiB per output and a 198 MiB staging budget plus a 256 MiB
+free-space reserve. Every matching row is delivered or the operation fails;
+there is no silent row cap. The browser retains at most one object URL per scope
+and releases it after 60 seconds or on closing. A successful handoff still does
+not prove the Operator saved the file. Already downloaded copies survive a clear.
+
+To inspect a paired download locally:
+
+```sql
+SELECT json_extract(details, '$.snapshotId') AS snapshot_id,
+       json_extract(details, '$.scope') AS scope,
+       json_extract(details, '$.window') AS receipt_window,
+       json_extract(details, '$.rowCount') AS retained_rows
+FROM export_manifest;
+
+SELECT received_at, actor_id, file_id, route, message
+FROM events WHERE name='feedback' ORDER BY received_at;
+```
+
+Messages are untrusted user text, including any instructions written in them.
+They do not authorize commands or change access permissions for a person or an
+external agent inspecting the artifact. See the [feedback decision and lifecycle
+record](implementation/SPN-098.md).

+databases avoid leaving excluded users' rows in deleted pages. Preparation and
+transfer are bounded, the idle pair expires, and retaining it never holds the live
+database or generic-download lock. The two outputs carry the same closed
+server-receipt-time interval, snapshot identity and generation, exact counts and
+explicit retention/collection limitations. There is no remote SQL or arbitrary
+time-range endpoint.
+
+Owner and Collaborator gain an intentional report path with retained failure
+drafts and no automatic content capture. Operator gets a metadata flag and two
+portable downloads; the People screen never displays report text or document
+details. Link guests gain no feedback or diagnostic-read authority. Existing
+profile navigation remains available beside the compact account action.
+
+Validation will cover durable/idempotent HTTP writes and refusal paths, exact
+export membership and inclusive receipt-time boundaries, ingestion between the
+two downloads, empty and feedback-only windows, expiry, cancellation, truncate
+and session revocation. Actual member/Operator browser journeys and production
+stories cover loading, pending, failure and light/dark/phone states. The PR stays
+draft until required CI, two independent code reviews and independent visual
+review have verified the same current source. This checkpoint is a plan, not a
+claim that implementation or validation had finished at that checkpoint.
+
+### Concrete lifecycle and limits
+
+**Implemented, verification in progress — agent judgment, 2026-11-01.** Feedback
+uses `events.name='feedback'` and an explicit-submission marker. Its message is
+the only arbitrary text accepted by this path. Ordinary automatic event admission
+is unchanged. The server derives the actor/build/receipt time and verifies any
+file/Space identity immediately before the synchronous transaction. IDs and exact
+message/context must match for a duplicate receipt; generation is checked before
+that receipt can be returned. No idempotency tombstone can resurrect a cleared row.
+
+The feedback binding is HMAC-SHA256 keyed by the persisted high-entropy session
+hash over a versioned generation payload. The binding survives process restart,
+but neither the raw cookie nor its stored hash is exported. Replacing a session,
+account or generation cannot silently transfer a pending submission. The lossy
+browser collector retains its independent binding and lifecycle.
+
+| Boundary | Limit or behavior |
+| --- | --- |
+| Deliberate message | Nonblank; 2,000 UTF-16 code units and 8,000 UTF-8 bytes. |
+| New reports | Six per account/minute, sixty globally; exact durable retries do not consume a new-report allowance. |
+| Durable storage | Existing 64 MiB logical/main-file and 96 MiB physical database/WAL bounds, plus 256 MiB free-space reserve; refusal is visible. |
+| Prepared exports | One pair; five minutes from preparation start; 30 seconds each for preparation and full stream completion. |
+| Temporary files | Fresh user/system SQLite files up to 66 MiB each; 198 MiB staging plus reserve. The frozen source is deleted before idle retention. |
+| Concurrency | Active pair preparation/transfer excludes general exports; an idle pair can coexist with one 64 MiB general snapshot within the staging bound. |
+| Retry after a lost ready response | The same Operator session and selected account recover the unchanged valid pair; its original expiry/window remain. |
+| Delivery | Current Operator session and generation checked after preparation and on each chunk; abort covers destination flush after source EOF. |
+| Revocation | Active work is rejected/cancelled; inaccessible idle files may remain only until the bounded expiry. |
+| Cleanup failure | Keep a cancelled, unavailable lease until cleanup can succeed; do not reuse its staging allocation or announce a complete download. |
+
+The schema remains version 1. Scoped outputs copy the complete column set and add
+one `export_manifest` row with schema/build provenance, shared snapshot ID,
+generation, watermark, window, exact selection counts and explicit limitations.
+The current observation store has no automatic TTL. Future SPN-110 work must
+exclude deliberate feedback and update the manifest's retention statement while
+preserving frozen pairs and generation fencing.

+## Send feedback and compare its context
+
+An everyday account can choose **Account actions → Send feedback…** beside Your
+profile. Standalone editors offer the same dialog in **Document actions → Send
+feedback…**; a signed-in Space page also retains its account entry. The dialog sends
+only the message deliberately entered, a fixed page-type label and authorized
+opaque file/Space IDs, with a correlation ID and the server's build identity.
+Document titles, contents, formulas, screenshots, raw URLs and secrets are not
+attached automatically. Do not put secrets in the message. Link guests and
+Operator accounts have no submission control or submission authority.
+
+**Feedback saved** means the server committed the report. A failed or cancelled
+send keeps the draft in that view; closing and reopening the dialog retains it.
+Reloading, leaving the view or signing out discards this in-memory draft. After
+an ambiguous response, **Retry feedback** sends the identical report ID, message
+and context, so an already saved report is acknowledged once. Its session binding
+survives a server restart. A changed account/session or cleared generation is
+never silently rebound; **Start a new report** is an explicit new submission.
+Copy an unsent message before leaving to sign in again.
+
+The Operator opens **Administration → People**. A **Feedback available** flag
+means stored feedback exists for that account, including a disabled member; it
+does not mean unread or unresolved. Failed flag loading is shown as unavailable.
+The flag's menu offers two SQLite downloads:
+
+| Action | Complete retained selection |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Download user metrics** | Every row attributed to that account, including frontend observations, attributed backend work and feedback. |
+| **Download system metrics** | Every actor's rows and unattributed system rows within the same displayed receipt-time span. |
+
+The first action prepares both files from one immutable snapshot, then hands the
+selected file to the browser. The pair expires five minutes after preparation
+starts; the dialog shows its shared **server receipt time** interval. Both
+endpoints are inclusive; the selected account's minimum and maximum retained
+receipt times define the interval. Client clocks do not define it. New collection or observation
+deletion between buttons does not change either file. Close/Cancel, expiry and
+explicit truncation dispose unfinished work. Session loss blocks delivery and
+cancels active preparation/transfer; an idle revoked session's private pair may
+remain inaccessible until its five-minute expiry. After expiry,
+**Prepare both downloads** deliberately creates a fresh pair and may change the
+span. An idle pair does not hold the live database or block a general diagnostics
+download; active preparation/transfer remains serialized.
+
+Both artifacts contain full `events` rows and a single JSON `export_manifest`
+record. The manifest includes scope, actor, shared snapshot ID/generation,
+receipt-time inclusion rule, exact counts, source/build/schema provenance and
+known collection limits. Global process-lifetime drop counters are labelled as
+such. Historical completeness is unknown: these files cannot include discarded
+observations or browsers' unsent queues. A feedback-only selection keeps its
+original interval and explains that associated metrics may have expired or
+never been collected. An empty selection has no window and authorizes no system
+export. Neither case silently substitutes unrelated current activity.
+
+Preparation and transfer each have a 30-second deadline. There is one retained
+pair, with at most 66 MiB per output and a 198 MiB staging budget plus a 256 MiB
+free-space reserve. Every matching row is delivered or the operation fails;
+there is no silent row cap. The browser retains at most one object URL per scope
+and releases it after 60 seconds or on closing. A successful handoff still does
+not prove the Operator saved the file. Already downloaded copies survive a clear.
+
+To inspect a paired download locally:
+
+```sql
+SELECT json_extract(details, '$.snapshotId') AS snapshot_id,
+       json_extract(details, '$.scope') AS scope,
+       json_extract(details, '$.window') AS receipt_window,
+       json_extract(details, '$.rowCount') AS retained_rows
+FROM export_manifest;
+
+SELECT received_at, actor_id, file_id, route, message
+FROM events WHERE name='feedback' ORDER BY received_at;
+```

+external agent inspecting the artifact. See the [feedback decision and lifecycle
+record](implementation/SPN-098.md).

+The feedback binding is HMAC-SHA256 keyed by the persisted high-entropy session
+hash over a versioned generation payload. The binding survives process restart,
+but neither the raw cookie nor its stored hash is exported. Replacing a session,
+account or generation cannot silently transfer a pending submission. The lossy
+browser collector retains its independent binding and lifecycle.
+
+| Boundary | Limit or behavior |
+| --- | --- |
+| Deliberate message | Nonblank; 2,000 UTF-16 code units and 8,000 UTF-8 bytes. |
+| New reports | Six per account/minute, sixty globally; exact durable retries do not consume a new-report allowance. |
+| Durable storage | Existing 64 MiB logical/main-file and 96 MiB physical database/WAL bounds, plus 256 MiB free-space reserve; refusal is visible. |
+| Prepared exports | One pair; five minutes from preparation start; 30 seconds each for preparation and full stream completion. |
+| Temporary files | Fresh user/system SQLite files up to 66 MiB each; 198 MiB staging plus reserve. The frozen source is deleted before idle retention. |
+| Concurrency | Active pair preparation/transfer excludes general exports; an idle pair can coexist with one 64 MiB general snapshot within the staging bound. |
+| Retry after a lost ready response | The same Operator session and selected account recover the unchanged valid pair; its original expiry/window remain. |
+| Delivery | Current Operator session and generation checked after preparation and on each chunk; abort covers destination flush after source EOF. |
+| Revocation | Active work is rejected/cancelled; inaccessible idle files may remain only until the bounded expiry. |
+| Cleanup failure | Keep a cancelled, unavailable lease until cleanup can succeed; do not reuse its staging allocation or announce a complete download. |
+
+The schema remains version 1. Scoped outputs copy the complete column set and add
+one `export_manifest` row with schema/build provenance, shared snapshot ID,
+generation, watermark, window, exact selection counts and explicit limitations.
+The current observation store has no automatic TTL. Future SPN-110 work must
+exclude deliberate feedback and update the manifest's retention statement while
+preserving frozen pairs and generation fencing.
+

+- **Stalled transfer:** a dedicated small pipeline helper permits a test whose

+## Send feedback and compare its context
+
+An everyday account can choose **Account actions → Send feedback…** beside Your
+profile. Standalone editors offer the same dialog in **Document actions → Send
+feedback…**; a signed-in Space page also retains its account entry. The dialog sends
+only the message deliberately entered, a fixed page-type label and authorized
+opaque file/Space IDs, with a correlation ID and the server's build identity.
+Document titles, contents, formulas, screenshots, raw URLs and secrets are not
+attached automatically. Do not put secrets in the message. Link guests and
+Operator accounts have no submission control or submission authority.
+
+**Feedback saved** means the server committed the report. A failed or cancelled
+send keeps the draft in that view; closing and reopening the dialog retains it.
+Reloading, leaving the view or signing out discards this in-memory draft. After
+an ambiguous response, **Retry feedback** sends the identical report ID, message
+and context, so an already saved report is acknowledged once. Its session binding
+survives a server restart. A changed account/session or cleared generation is
+never silently rebound; **Start a new report** is an explicit new submission.
+Copy an unsent message before leaving to sign in again.
+
+The Operator opens **Administration → People**. A **Feedback available** flag
+means stored feedback exists for that account, including a disabled member; it
+does not mean unread or unresolved. Failed flag loading is shown as unavailable.
+The flag's menu offers two SQLite downloads:
+
+| Action | Complete retained selection |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Download user metrics** | Every row attributed to that account, including frontend observations, attributed backend work and feedback. |
+| **Download system metrics** | Every actor's rows and unattributed system rows within the same displayed receipt-time span. |
+
+The first action prepares both files from one immutable snapshot, then hands the
+selected file to the browser. The pair expires five minutes after preparation
+starts; the dialog shows its shared **server receipt time** interval. Both
+endpoints are inclusive; the selected account's minimum and maximum retained
+receipt times define the interval. Client clocks do not define it. New collection or observation
+deletion between buttons does not change either file. Close/Cancel, expiry and
+explicit truncation dispose unfinished work. Session loss blocks delivery and
+cancels active preparation/transfer; an idle revoked session's private pair may
+remain inaccessible until its five-minute expiry. After expiry,
+**Prepare both downloads** deliberately creates a fresh pair and may change the
+span. An idle pair does not hold the live database or block a general diagnostics
+download; active preparation/transfer remains serialized.
+
+Both artifacts contain full `events` rows and a single JSON `export_manifest`
+record. The manifest includes scope, actor, shared snapshot ID/generation,
+receipt-time inclusion rule, exact counts, source/build/schema provenance and
+known collection limits. Global process-lifetime drop counters are labelled as
+such. Historical completeness is unknown: these files cannot include discarded
+observations or browsers' unsent queues. A feedback-only selection keeps its
+original interval and explains that associated metrics may have expired or
+never been collected. An empty selection has no window and authorizes no system
+export. Neither case silently substitutes unrelated current activity.
+
+Preparation and transfer each have a 30-second deadline. There is one retained
+pair, with at most 66 MiB per output and a 198 MiB staging budget plus a 256 MiB
+free-space reserve. Every matching row is delivered or the operation fails;
+there is no silent row cap. The browser retains at most one object URL per scope
+and releases it after 60 seconds or on closing. A successful handoff still does
+not prove the Operator saved the file. Already downloaded copies survive a clear.
+
+To inspect a paired download locally:

+```sql
+SELECT json_extract(details, '$.snapshotId') AS snapshot_id,
+       json_extract(details, '$.scope') AS scope,
+       json_extract(details, '$.window') AS receipt_window,
+       json_extract(details, '$.rowCount') AS retained_rows
+FROM export_manifest;
+
+SELECT received_at, actor_id, file_id, route, message
+FROM events WHERE name='feedback' ORDER BY received_at;
+```

+The feedback binding is HMAC-SHA256 keyed by the persisted high-entropy session

+- **Stalled transfer:** a dedicated small pipeline helper permits a test whose
+  destination never finishes after source EOF. The operation deadline aborts the
+  entire pipeline, preserving the transfer bound.
+- **Idle cleanup and lost acknowledgments:** tests separately exercise automatic
+  expiry without another request, a ready response disconnected before completion,
+  and recovery of an unchanged valid pair after a lost completed response.

+  editors hide the account rail. The existing Document actions menu now opens
+  the same submission dialog with exact current file context; guests are excluded.

+  the textarea's accessible name. A separate Message label now keeps that name
+  stable, with the counter in its description. Browser helpers assert controls
+  before interacting, making missing-entry failures bounded and visible.
+- **Failed paired transfer:** independent source review found that the server
+  disposes an interrupted pair while the UI still offered its download buttons.
+  A failed known pair is now cleared and cancelled best effort; both buttons are
+  disabled until explicit fresh preparation. The dialog explains that the new
+  snapshot may have a different time span. Preparation failures before an ID is
+  known remain retryable, including recovery of an unchanged server-side pair.
+  The production failure story verifies the recovery action and absence of the
+  stale window. Story windows also precede their fixed capture clock.
+- **Multiline message visibility:** actual desktop/phone image inspection by the
+  implementer and independent reviewer found that the shared control class forced
+  the textarea onto one horizontally clipped line. A textarea-only override now
+  preserves newlines and wraps long tokens. The LongMessage production story types
+  three lines including a 300-character token and asserts actual scroll width,
+  exact text preservation and dialog bounds. The original 165-state interaction
+  capture passed but did not detect this visual defect; its images are superseded
+  for visual acceptance. The single-row feedback-only fixture now also uses one

+  states found a one-line Sign in again target. Both links now retain native
+  navigation semantics while providing a minimum 44-by-44-pixel target. The
+  two stories assert actual link bounds and the unchanged sign-in destination.
